title: Derivative chromosome 9 — t(9;22)
clinical_history: Identify anatomy on der(9) from t(9;22), then reconstruct it from 9pter through 9q34 plus distal 22q. This is the reciprocal partner of the Philadelphia chromosome. Demonstration map only.
hints: der(9) keeps 9pter through 9q34, then continues with 22q11.2→22qter.
The centromere of this derivative is still a chromosome 9 centromere.
The balanced study is written t(9;22)(q34;q11.2); der(22) is the small Philadelphia chromosome.
anatomy_hints: The centromere matches chromosome 9. Distal long-arm bands do not.
Name the rearrangement class and the two chromosomes whose q-arm bands meet on this map.
explanation: The derivative is assembled by truncating the chromosome 9 map after 9q34 and appending distal 22q segments. Together with der(22), that models the reciprocal t(9;22) of chronic myeloid leukemia.
plain_language_interpretation: der(9)t(9;22)(q34;q11.2), the reciprocal partner of the Philadelphia chromosome.
